papers.title_en: On the approximation of posterior laws in compound loss models by conditional Wasserstein GANs
papers.authors: Aleksandar Arandjelovic, Pavel V. Shevchenko, George Tzougas
papers.evidence: 基于条件 Wasserstein GAN 的摊销后验逼近
papers.tldr: 复合损失模型的贝叶斯推断常需跨保单、场景和先验重复计算，非共轭情形下代价高昂。本文将其视为摊销后验近似问题，构造以充分统计量、先验均值和变异系数及混合权重为条件的Wasserstein GAN，用单一生成器近似泊松强度与Pareto形状参数的后验。经仿真校准与解析/数值/MCMC对比验证，应用于极端巨灾损失数据生成滚动一年期后验预测，揭示重尾与先验族不确定性对聚合尾风险的影响。
papers.abstract_en: Bayesian inference in compound loss models must often be repeated across policies, market scenarios, and prior specifications. Outside conjugate cases, this may require repeated numerical integration or Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). We formulate this problem as amortized posterior approximation and construct a conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial network conditioned on sufficient statistics, prior mean and coefficient of variation, and mixture weights of prior families. Notably, a single shared generator is able to approximate the posterior laws of both the Poisson intensity and the Pareto shape parameter under mixtures of Gamma, inverse-Gaussian, and lognormal priors. We assess the approximation by simulation-based calibration and by comparisons with analytical posteriors, deterministic quadrature, and extensive MCMC simulations. In an application to data on extreme natural catastrophe losses, we produce rolling one-year posterior predictive distributions, and examine the effects of heavy-tailed severity and prior-family uncertainty on aggregate tail risk.

papers.title_en: Forecasting Multiple Observables with SCROLL: Score-Trained Uncertainty for Stochastic Dynamics
papers.evidence: 用逐任务末层信念与得分训练似然对随机动力学预测不确定性建模，直接面向深度学习中的不确定性量化。
papers.tldr: 预测随机动力系统需多个可观测量的似然，标准多任务方法依赖损失平衡调参。本文提出SCROLL，在共享骨干上为各任务构建自由路由的最后一层信念，将单位相关损失缩放吸收为似然参数同步学习。在OU过程恢复解析核，在异方差Lorenz-63和空气质量数据上状态与regime任务取得最佳单次NLL且校准匹配，成本远低于调参网格。实现了无需手动调参的多任务不确定性预测。
papers.abstract_en: Forecasting a stochastic dynamical system rarely means a single number: one wants several observables---future state, threshold event, regime label---each with its own likelihood. Standard multi-task recipes balance per-task losses, tuned or learned. We instead compose the observables' likelihoods in per-task free-routed last-layer beliefs on a shared backbone; this absorbs unit-dependent loss scaling into likelihood parameters learned in the same gradient pass. Stochastic dynamics supply what static benchmarks cannot: computable ground truth for the predictive variance. Results land where theory puts them: on the well-specified, homoscedastic Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process the learned predictive law recovers the analytic kernel and correctly specified baselines tie. On heteroscedastic systems (stochastic Lorenz-63, real air-quality data) the belief's input-dependent variance separates: best single-run NLL on the state and regime tasks, calibration matched only by arms whose NLL it beats, at a fraction of the tuned grids' cost. On the real series the state margin holds across five rolling origins.
